description: §19.8.3 / §19.4.3 (S451 R11) — a `?{}` query handled by `!{}` INSIDE an expression: the condition of an `if` in a server function (RUNTIME, sqlEngine:"real"). `notes` has a row → the condition is the row (truthy) → "found"; `empties` is empty → `not` → "absent"; `gone` is declared but never created, so the query fails to run → the `_ :> not` arm's value → "absent". Pre-S454 the build failed with E-CODEGEN-INVALID-LOGIC: the `!{` reached the emitted JS raw, because a `!{}` written anywhere but the end of a whole statement was never parsed as a handler.
rationale: §19.8.4: "A `?{}` query SHALL be a failable expression in every context. Outside a `!` function it SHALL be handled at the site with a `!{}` handler or a `match`". §19.4.3: a handler is in a value position in "an operand of an operator … — any position whose result is read", where every arm yields a value of the success type (`.get()` yields `Row | not`, so `_ :> not` yields a value).
